We cannot rely on the government and the US constitution to protect our privacy and our personal data, thoughts, habits, and secrets. In order to regain some privacy in the age of the internet it is helpful to know about the privacy tools available to us.

Today a schizoid hivemind of pundits claim that no anonymity exists on the internet. These claims can be quickly debunked, even with a few free browser plugins like ghostery, and NoScript, we can easily hide our identity. I will highlight a number of various methods for doing this and much more.

There are many ways to remain anonymous, encrypt and obfuscate internet traffic, and completely hide your internet activities from your ISP and from anyone else. In fact, fhere are a number of fundamental technologies that are built into the internet protocols specifically designed to encrypt digital traffic and mask IP addresses.

The ability to remain anonymous and private on the internet depends on the user's activities. Those who behave a certain way on line and use certain services will have no privacy. While those who behave another way and use other services, can be very very hard to identify, harder to identify now in many ways then ever in communications history.

**Privacy Guarding Browser Plugins**

Here are a list of essential plugins to prevent scripts running the background of websites from tracking you.

Ghostery - A great plugin dedicated to blocking unwanted objects imbedded in web pages. - Ghostery is available for chrome and firefox, and is a great way to preserve your privacy online. It blooks data collection sites, tracking sides, nefarious advertisers and other unwanted domains.

Privacy Badger -- From the website - Privacy Badger is a browser add-on that stops advertisers and other third-party trackers from secretly tracking where you go and what pages you look at on the web.

Ublock - Fast and lightweight adblocker.

** VPNs **

The easiest solution is to use a private VPN to encrypt your torrenting. The ISP can only log that your connecting to the VPN. The swarm can only see your VPN assigned IP. This shouldn't be too hard; and most VPN providors will have step-by-step guides somewhere on their sites. Use a private VPN. Don't use a free VPN. Use OpenVPN https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenVPN. There are numerous benefits to having all of your traffic encrypted.

**VPS **

It's a bit more involved but you can use a VPS https://goo.gl/kNdEj as a seedbox https://goo.gl/l7pCd.

* Extensive list of seedbox providers https://goo.gl/pA8Qa

**Retroshare**

Retroshare https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retroshare is a special little program, but can be little tricky. It really should be used as a genuine friend to genuine friend network F2F Networks https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friend-to-friend . But if you do have interesting friends, online or in person, Retroshare offers encrypted communication and filesharing.

* Unofficial Retroshare Wiki: Adding Friends http://retroshare.wikidot.com/en:adding-friends If you need help with this, send me a PM.

**I2P**

I2P https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I2p I2P is quickly growing and could replace TOR as the largest encrypted, decentralized intranet over the public internet. Definitely something to keep an eye on. It is also Open Source, p2p and free. I think it has the most long term value but at this point needs another wave of early adopters.

I2P popularity has been growing and has modern features like the ability to torrents within this darknet.

* "An easy way for people to learn about i2p is **tails**. i2p is built in tails and configured by default.

* Netizens in China use tails on their computer to circumvent the "great firewall of china"

**TOR** - The Onion Router

TOR is the most infamous darknet and is a controversial and very successful anonymizing network that originated from the United States Naval Research Laboratory. TOR is already widely used. History of TOR https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tor_%28anonymity_network%29#History

**FreeNet**

Freenet is a peer-to-peer platform for censorship-resistant communication. It uses a decentralized distributed data store to keep and deliver information, and has a suite of free software for publishing and communicating on the Web without fear of censorship.

Freenet's explicit goal is to promote freedom of speech on the internet. Freenet is not as widely used as other darkweb networks but it is extremely secure and few vulnerabilities since it has been highly refined since its first release in 2000.

Even though improving trout habitat in November in Wisconsin is hella cold, I would do it again if I could. That job inspired a life long respect for the outdoors.

A little late, but I used to work the cafeteria in an auction house. The cool thing about it is that this auction house used to be an elementary school in the early 1900s. Classrooms still had books, lockers still intact, and some writing on a chalkboard so old that it can't easily be erased. None of the auction goers were allowed to go upstairs, but I personally knew the owner of the place, and she let me explore during the auction downtime. It was really surreal, seeing a place taken out of time like that.
